q: 11 दिसंबर 1946 को भारत की संविधान सभा का स्थायी अध्यक्ष किसे निर्वाचित किया गया था?
e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946. (11 दिसंबर 1946 को डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद को संविधान सभा का स्थायी अध्यक्ष चुना गया।) Exam Boosters: (1) Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha served as the temporary (pro-tem) President at the first sitting on 9 December 1946 following the French practice. (2) H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents, while Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor. (3) Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee (constituted on 29 August 1947). (4) Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 (adopted 22 January 1947).
qe: Who was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly of India on 11 December 1946?

q:
सूची-I (संवैधानिक विशेषता) को सूची-II (स्रोत देश) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — (a) कनाडा
2. सशक्त केंद्र के साथ संघ — (b) आयरलैंड
3. समवर्ती सूची व संयुक्त बैठक — (c) दक्षिण अफ्रीका
4. संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया — (d) ऑस्ट्रेलिया
e: DPSP is borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1-b); Federation with a strong Centre and Residuary powers with Centre come from Canada (2-a); Concurrent List and Joint Sitting (Art 108) come from Australia (3-d); and Constitutional Amendment procedure (Art 368) is borrowed from South Africa (4-c). (अतः सही सुमेलन 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, and Impeachment of President come from the USA. (2) Parliamentary system, Single Citizenship, Rule of Law, and Writs come from the UK. (3) Fundamental Duties and Ideals of Justice come from the USSR (Russia). (4) Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency comes from the Weimar Constitution of Germany.
qe:
Match List-I (Constitutional Feature) with List-II (Borrowed Source):
1. Directive Principles of State Policy (नीति निदेशक तत्व) — (a) Canada
2. Federation with a Strong Centre (सशक्त केंद्र के साथ संघ) — (b) Ireland
3. Concurrent List & Joint Sitting (समवर्ती सूची व संयुक्त बैठक) — (c) South Africa
4. Procedure of Constitutional Amendment (संविधान संशोधन प्रक्रिया) — (d) Australia

q: 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में कौन-से तीन शब्द जोड़े गए थे?
e: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 ("Mini-Constitution") amended the Preamble for the only time so far, inserting three words: Socialist (समाजवादी), Secular (पंथनिरपेक्ष), and Integrity (अखंडता). Exam Boosters: (1) In Berubari Union Case (1960), SC held Preamble is NOT part of the Constitution. (2) In Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973), SC overruled Berubari and held Preamble IS an integral part and can be amended without altering the Basic Structure. (3) In LIC of India Case (1995), SC reaffirmed Preamble as an integral part. (4) The Preamble mentions 3 types of Justice (Social, Economic, Political) and 5 types of Liberty (Thought, Expression, Belief, Faith, Worship).
qe: Which three words were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

q: भारतीय संविधान की निम्नलिखित अनुसूचियों में से कौन-सी अपने विषय के साथ सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
o: चौथी अनुसूची — राज्यसभा में सीटों का आवंटन
छठी अनुसूची — असम, मेघालय, त्रिपुरा, मिजोरम के जनजातीय क्षेत्र
दसवीं अनुसूची — पंचायतों की शक्तियाँ व उत्तरदायित्व
e: The Tenth Schedule deals with Anti-Defection Law (दलबदल विरोधी कानून), added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985—NOT Panchayats. Panchayats are listed in the Eleventh Schedule (added by the 73rd Amendment, 1992, containing 29 subjects). Exam Boosters: (1) Ninth Schedule (land reforms) was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951; in I. R. Coelho Case (2007), SC held laws placed in it after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review. (2) Twelfth Schedule (Municipalities, 18 subjects) was added by the 74th Amendment, 1992. (3) Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages; Sindhi (21st), Konkani-Manipuri-Nepali (71st), and Bodo-Dogri-Maithili-Santhali (92nd) brought it to 22.
qe: Which of the following Schedules of the Indian Constitution is NOT correctly matched with its subject matter?
oe: Fourth Schedule — Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha
Sixth Schedule — Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
Tenth Schedule — Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats

q:
भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: प्रस्तावना गैर-न्यायोचित (non-justiciable) है और यह न तो विधायिका की शक्ति का स्रोत है और न ही उसकी शक्तियों पर प्रतिबंध है।
कथन II: प्रस्तावना में स्वतंत्रता, समता और बंधुता के आदर्श अमेरिकी क्रांति से प्रेरित थे।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Statement I is correct—the Preamble cannot be enforced directly in a court of law and neither confers nor restricts legislative power. Statement II is incorrect because Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity were inspired by the French Revolution (1789), while Social, Economic, and Political Justice came from the Russian Revolution (1917). (अतः केवल कथन I सही है।) Exam Boosters: (1) N. A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the "Identity Card of the Constitution". (2) K. M. Munshi called it the "Horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic". (3) The Preamble states the date of adoption as 26 November 1949 (Miti Margashirsha Shukla Saptami, Samvat 2006 Vikram).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:
Statement I: The Preamble is non-justiciable and neither a source of power to the legislature nor a prohibition upon its powers.
Statement II: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble were inspired by the American Revolution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस भाग और किन अनुच्छेदों में नागरिकता (Citizenship) से संबंधित प्रावधान निहित हैं?
e: Citizenship provisions are placed in Part II (Articles 5 to 11) of the Constitution. (नागरिकता के प्रावधान भाग II के अनुच्छेद 5 से 11 में हैं।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 9 states that a person who voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship automatically ceases to be an Indian citizen (Single Citizenship). (2) Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law, under which the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted. (3) Five modes of acquiring citizenship under the 1955 Act: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, and Incorporation of Territory. (4) Three modes of losing citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, and Deprivation.
qe: Under which Part and Articles of the Indian Constitution are the provisions relating to Citizenship contained?

q: संविधान सभा की निम्नलिखित में से किस समिति की अध्यक्षता सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल ने की थी?
e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal Areas. (सरदार पटेल प्रांतीय संविधान समिति के अध्यक्ष थे।) Exam Boosters: (1) Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee, Union Constitution Committee, and States Committee. (2) Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure Committee and Steering Committee. (3) J. B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee, and H. C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee. (4) The Constitution took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days across 11 sessions to complete.
qe: Which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 3 के अंतर्गत संसद किसी विद्यमान राज्य की सीमाओं या नाम में परिवर्तन कर सकती है:
o: अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत विशेष बहुमत से
राज्य विधानमंडल से परामर्श के बिना अध्यादेश द्वारा
विशेष बहुमत व आधे राज्यों के अनुसमर्थन से
राष्ट्रपति की पूर्व सिफारिश के साथ साधारण बहुमत से
e: Under Article 3, a bill altering state boundaries/names requires the President's prior recommendation and referral to the concerned State Legislature (whose views are NOT binding on Parliament), and is passed by a simple majority. Article 4 explicitly clarifies that laws under Articles 2 and 3 are NOT deemed constitutional amendments under Article 368. (अतः साधारण बहुमत व राष्ट्रपति की पूर्व सिफारिश से।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 1 describes India as a "Union of States" (not Federation), implying states have no right to secede. (2) However, ceding Indian territory to a foreign state requires a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368 (Berubari Case 1960; 100th Amendment 2015 for India-Bangladesh enclave swap). (3) States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Fazl Ali Commission) created 14 states and 6 UTs.
qe: Under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament can alter the boundaries or name of an existing state by:
oe: Presidential Ordinance without consulting the State Legislature
Special majority plus ratification by half the states
Simple majority with President's prior recommendation

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद "अस्पृश्यता" (Untouchability) का अंत करता है और इसका किसी भी रूप में आचरण निषिद्ध करता है?
e: Article 17 abolishes Untouchability and makes enforcement of any disability arising out of it a punishable offence. (अनुच्छेद 17 अस्पृश्यता का उन्मूलन करता है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 17 is an absolute right available against both the State and private individuals. (2) Parliament enacted the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 (earlier Untouchability Offences Act) and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 under Article 35 to enforce it. (3) Article 15 prohibits discrimination on 5 grounds (religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth); Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment; Article 18 abolishes titles (except military and academic).
qe: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes "Untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form?

q: डॉ. बी. आर. अम्बेडकर ने किस अनुच्छेद को "भारतीय संविधान का हृदय और आत्मा" कहा था?
e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the "very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it" because it empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. (डॉ. अम्बेडकर ने अनुच्छेद 32 को संविधान की आत्मा कहा।) Exam Boosters: (1) Under Article 32, SC can issue 5 writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. (2) Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right and part of the Basic Structure. (3) High Courts have wider writ jurisdiction under Article 226 (can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights). (4) Note: Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava called the Preamble the "soul of the Constitution".
qe: Which Article was described by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as the "Heart and Soul of the Indian Constitution"?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से मौलिक अधिकार केवल भारत के नागरिकों को प्राप्त हैं, विदेशियों को नहीं?
e: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are exclusively reserved for Indian citizens. (अनुच्छेद 15, 16, 19, 29 तथा 30 केवल भारतीय नागरिकों को प्राप्त हैं।) Exam Boosters: (1) Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, and 28 are available to both citizens and foreigners (except enemy aliens for Art 22). (2) Easy memory trick for citizen-only rights: "15-16-19-29-30". (3) By the 44th Amendment (1978), Articles 20 and 21 can NEVER be suspended even during a National Emergency (Art 359). (4) Right to Property (Art 31 & 19(1)(f)) was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment and made a legal right under Article 300A.
qe: Which of the following Fundamental Rights are available ONLY to citizens of India and NOT to foreigners?

q: किस ऐतिहासिक निर्णय में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने "निजता के अधिकार" (Right to Privacy) को अनुच्छेद 21 के अंतर्गत एक मौलिक अधिकार घोषित किया?
e: A 9-judge Constitution Bench in Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) unanimously held that Right to Privacy is a Fundamental Right protected under Article 21, overruling M. P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962). (पुट्टास्वामी वाद 2017 में निजता के अधिकार को अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत मौलिक अधिकार माना गया।) Exam Boosters: (1) Maneka Gandhi Case (1978) expanded Art 21 from "procedure established by law" to "due process of law" (fair, just, and reasonable). (2) Vishaka Case (1997) laid down guidelines against sexual harassment at workplace (later POSH Act, 2013). (3) Navtej Singh Johar Case (2018) decriminalized consensual adult same-sex relations under IPC Section 377.
qe: In which landmark judgment did the Supreme Court declare the "Right to Privacy" to be an intrinsic Fundamental Right under Article 21?
oe: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978
Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, 2018

q:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 20 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: अनुच्छेद 20(1) के अंतर्गत भूतलक्षी दंड विधियों से संरक्षण आपराधिक और दीवानी दोनों कानूनों पर लागू होता है।
कथन II: अनुच्छेद 20(2) के अंतर्गत दोहरे दंड से संरक्षण केवल न्यायालय या न्यायिक अधिकरण की कार्यवाही पर लागू होता है, विभागीय जाँच पर नहीं।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Statement I is incorrect because Article 20(1) prohibits retrospective criminal laws only; civil and tax laws CAN be enacted retrospectively. Statement II is correct—Article 20(2) bars prosecution and punishment twice before a court/judicial tribunal, not administrative/departmental proceedings. (केवल कथन II सही है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 20(3) protects against self-incrimination (no accused can be compelled to be a witness against himself). (2) In Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010), SC held involuntary narco-analysis, polygraph, and brain-mapping violate Art 20(3) and Art 21. (3) Article 20 cannot be suspended during National Emergency.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 20 of the Indian Constitution:
Statement I: Protection against ex-post-facto laws under Article 20(1) applies to both criminal and civil laws.
Statement II: Protection against double jeopardy under Article 20(2) applies only to proceedings before a court of law or judicial tribunal, not departmental inquiries.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद राज्य को ग्राम पंचायतों का गठन करने और उन्हें स्वशासन की शक्तियाँ प्रदान करने का निर्देश देता है?
e: Article 40 (a Gandhian DPSP) directs the State to organize Village Panchayats as units of self-government, later given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992. (अनुच्छेद 40 ग्राम पंचायतों के गठन से संबंधित है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 39A (added by 42nd Amendment, 1976): Equal justice and free legal aid. (2) Article 43: Living wage and promotion of cottage industries; Article 43B (97th Amendment, 2011): Promotion of co-operative societies. (3) Article 44: Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India. (4) Article 50: Separation of Judiciary from Executive.
qe: Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to organize Village Panchayats and endow them with powers of self-government?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा नीति निदेशक तत्व 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा नहीं जोड़ा गया था?
o: समान न्याय व निःशुल्क विधिक सहायता
उद्योगों के प्रबंधन में कर्मकारों की भागीदारी
आय, प्रतिष्ठा व अवसर की असमानता कम करना
e: Article 38(2) was added by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, NOT the 42nd Amendment. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added four DPSPs: Art 39(f) (healthy development of children), Art 39A, Art 43A, and Art 48A. (अनुच्छेद 38(2) को 44वें संशोधन 1978 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था।) Exam Boosters: (1) 86th Amendment (2002) modified Article 45 to cover early childhood care and education for children below 6 years. (2) 97th Amendment (2011) added Article 43B for cooperative societies. (3) DPSPs (Part IV, Art 36–51) are non-justiciable (Art 37) yet fundamental in the governance of the country.
qe: Which of the following Directive Principles was NOT added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
oe: Article 39A — Equal justice and free legal aid
Article 43A — Participation of workers in management of industries
Article 48A — Protection and improvement of environment and forests
Article 38(2) — Minimizing inequalities in income, status, and opportunities

q:
सूची-I (नीति निदेशक अनुच्छेद) को सूची-II (प्रावधान) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. अनुच्छेद 41 — (a) समान नागरिक संहिता
2. अनुच्छेद 44 — (b) काम, शिक्षा व लोक सहायता का अधिकार
3. अनुच्छेद 48 — (c) अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति व सुरक्षा की अभिवृद्धि
4. अनुच्छेद 51 — (d) कृषि एवं पशुपालन का संगठन
e: Article 41 covers right to work, education, and public assistance in old age/sickness (1-b); Article 44 mandates Uniform Civil Code (2-a); Article 48 covers agriculture, animal husbandry, and prohibiting cow slaughter (3-d); and Article 51 deals with international peace and India's foreign policy foundation (4-c). Exam Boosters: (1) Article 42: Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief. (2) Article 47: Raising level of nutrition and prohibition of intoxicating drinks/drugs. (3) Article 49: Protection of monuments and places of national importance.
qe:
Match List-I (DPSP Article) with List-II (Provision):
1. Article 41 — (a) Uniform Civil Code
2. Article 44 — (b) Right to work, education, and public assistance
3. Article 48 — (c) Promotion of international peace and security
4. Article 51 — (d) Organization of agriculture and animal husbandry

q: किस ऐतिहासिक वाद में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने सभी नीति निदेशक तत्वों की मौलिक अधिकारों पर पूर्ण प्राथमिकता को रद्द कर कहा कि संविधान भाग III और भाग IV के संतुलन की आधारशिला पर टिका है?
e: In Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980), the SC invalidated the 42nd Amendment's extension of Art 31C to all DPSPs and ruled that harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSP is part of the Basic Structure. (मिनर्वा मिल्स वाद 1980 में मौलिक अधिकारों व नीति निदेशक तत्वों के संतुलन को मूल ढाँचा घोषित किया गया।) Exam Boosters: (1) Champakam Dorairajan (1951): FRs prevail over DPSP in case of conflict, leading to the 1st Amendment. (2) Golaknath (1967): Parliament cannot abridge FRs (overruled by 24th Amendment & Kesavananda Bharati 1973). (3) Indra Sawhney (1992): Upheld 27% OBC reservation with creamy layer exclusion and 50% cap.
qe: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court strike down the absolute primacy of all DPSPs over Fundamental Rights and hold that the Constitution rests on the bedrock of balance between Part III and Part IV?

q: भारतीय संविधान के भाग IVA (अनुच्छेद 51A) में मौलिक कर्तव्यों को किस समिति की सिफारिश पर शामिल किया गया था?
e: On the recommendation of the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee (1976), the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added Part IVA and Article 51A with 10 Fundamental Duties (borrowed from USSR). (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति की सिफारिश पर 42वें संशोधन 1976 द्वारा 10 मौलिक कर्तव्य जोड़े गए।) Exam Boosters: (1) The 11th Fundamental Duty [Art 51A(k)—parents/guardians to provide education opportunities to children aged 6–14] was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. (2) The Verma Committee (1999) identified legal provisions already existing to enforce Fundamental Duties. (3) Swaran Singh Committee had recommended 8 duties and penalty for non-compliance, plus a duty to pay taxes—the latter two were NOT accepted.
qe: Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 51A के अंतर्गत मौलिक कर्तव्य के रूप में सूचीबद्ध नहीं है?
o: वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण, मानववाद व ज्ञानार्जन की भावना का विकास करना
सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की सुरक्षा करना और हिंसा से दूर रहना
सार्वजनिक चुनावों में मतदान करना और नियमित कर चुकाना
वनों व वन्यजीवों सहित प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा करना
e: Voting in elections and paying taxes are NOT Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. (मतदान करना और कर चुकाना अनुच्छेद 51A में मौलिक कर्तव्य नहीं हैं।) Exam Boosters: (1) Art 51A(g): Protect natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife. (2) Art 51A(h): Develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry and reform. (3) Art 51A(i): Safeguard public property and abjure violence. (4) Fundamental Duties apply ONLY to Indian citizens (not foreigners) and are non-justiciable unless backed by parliamentary law.
qe: Which of the following is NOT listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution?
oe: To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To cast vote in public elections and pay taxes regularly
To protect and improve the natural environment including forests and wildlife

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन अनुच्छेद 54 के तहत भारत के राष्ट्रपति के निर्वाचन में भाग लेता है, परंतु अनुच्छेद 61 के तहत राष्ट्रपति के महाभियोग में भाग नहीं लेता?
e: Elected MLAs of States and UTs of Delhi & Puducherry vote in the Presidential election (Art 54), but do NOT participate in impeachment (Art 61). Conversely, nominated MPs of both Houses do NOT vote in election, yet DO participate in impeachment! (राज्य विधानसभाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्य निर्वाचन में भाग लेते हैं, महाभियोग में नहीं।) Exam Boosters: (1) Impeachment (Art 61) requires a resolution passed by a 2/3rd majority of the TOTAL membership of each House, with 14 days' prior notice signed by 1/4th of members. (2) Ground for impeachment: "Violation of the Constitution". (3) Election disputes of President/VP are decided solely by the Supreme Court (Art 71).
qe: Who among the following participates in the election of the President of India under Article 54, but does NOT participate in the impeachment of the President under Article 61?
oe: Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 72 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति की क्षमादान शक्ति "लघुकरण" (Commutation) का क्या अर्थ है?
o: दोषी को दंड व दोषसिद्धि दोनों से पूर्णतः मुक्त करना
दंड के एक रूप को हल्के रूप में बदलना
दंड की प्रकृति बदले बिना उसकी अवधि कम करना
मृत्युदंड के निष्पादन पर अस्थायी रोक लगाना
e: Commutation (लघुकरण) means substituting a harsher form of punishment with a lighter character—for example, changing a death sentence to rigorous imprisonment. (लघुकरण का अर्थ दंड के स्वरूप को बदलकर हल्का करना है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Pardon (क्षमा) = Option A; Remission (परिहार) = Option C (e.g., 5 years RI reduced to 2 years RI); Reprieve (प्रविलंबन) = Option D; Respite (विराम) = lesser sentence due to special facts like pregnancy/disability. (2) Governor (Art 161) has similar powers EXCEPT cannot pardon a death sentence or court-martial punishment (though Governor can suspend/remit/commute a death sentence).
qe: Under Article 72 of the Indian Constitution, what does the President's pardoning power of "Commutation" (लघुकरण) mean?
oe: Completely absolving the convict of both sentence and conviction
Substituting one form of punishment for a lighter form
Reducing the period of sentence without changing its character
Staying the execution of a death sentence temporarily

q: अनुच्छेद 123 के अंतर्गत संसद की स्वीकृति के बिना भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा प्रख्यापित अध्यादेश (Ordinance) की अधिकतम संभावित अवधि कितनी होती है?
e: An Ordinance must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 6 weeks of its reassembly. Since the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is 6 months (Art 85), the maximum possible life of an Ordinance without approval is 6 months + 6 weeks. (अध्यादेश की अधिकतम अवधि 6 माह 6 सप्ताह हो सकती है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Governor's ordinance power is under Article 213. (2) In D. C. Wadhwa Case (1987), SC held successive repromulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature is a "fraud on the Constitution". (3) In R. C. Cooper Case (1970), SC held President's satisfaction in issuing an ordinance is subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fide.
qe: Under Article 123, what is the maximum possible life of an Ordinance promulgated by the President of India without parliamentary approval?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद (प्रधानमंत्री सहित) का कुल आकार लोकसभा की कुल सदस्य संख्या के 15% तक सीमित कर दिया गया?
e: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Article 75(1A) capping the Union Council of Ministers at 15% of Lok Sabha strength, and Article 164(1A) capping State Councils at 15% of Assembly strength (minimum 12 ministers including CM). (91वें संशोधन 2003 द्वारा मंत्रिपरिषद का आकार 15% सीमित किया गया।) Exam Boosters: (1) Under Art 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (not Parliament). (2) Under Art 75(2), ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (individual responsibility). (3) A non-MP appointed as Minister must become an MP within 6 months [Art 75(5)].
qe: By which Constitutional Amendment was the total size of the Union Council of Ministers (including the Prime Minister) capped at 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?

q: किस संसदीय समिति में सभी 30 सदस्य केवल लोकसभा से होते हैं और राज्यसभा का कोई प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं होता?
e: The Estimates Committee (प्राक्कलन समिति), often called the "continuous economy committee", is the largest parliamentary committee with 30 members, all elected exclusively from the Lok Sabha via proportional representation for a 1-year term. Exam Boosters: (1) Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS), and by convention since 1967 its Chairperson is from the Opposition; it examines CAG audit reports. (2) Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) also has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS), created in 1964 on Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation. (3) No minister can be a member of PAC, Estimates Committee, or COPU.
qe: Which Parliamentary Committee consists exclusively of 30 members drawn ONLY from the Lok Sabha, with no representation from the Rajya Sabha?

q: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 100(3) के अनुसार संसद के किसी भी सदन की बैठक गठित करने के लिए आवश्यक गणपूर्ति (Quorum) कितनी है?
o: कुल सदस्य संख्या का दसवाँ भाग
e: Under Article 100(3), the quorum for Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha is 1/10th of the total membership of the House, including the Presiding Officer (55 members in Lok Sabha out of 543/545, and 25 members in Rajya Sabha out of 245). (संसद के किसी सदन की गणपूर्ति कुल सदस्य संख्या का 1/10 होती है।) Exam Boosters: (1) For State Legislatures (Art 189), quorum is 10 members or 1/10th of total membership, whichever is greater. (2) Under Art 100(1), the Speaker/Chairman exercises a casting vote (निर्णायक मत) only in the case of a tie.
qe: What is the quorum required to constitute a sitting of either House of Parliament under Article 100(3) of the Constitution?

q: संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत राज्यसभा राष्ट्रीय हित में राज्य सूची के किसी विषय पर कानून बनाने के लिए संसद को अधिकृत कर सकती है?
e: Under Article 249, if Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting declaring it necessary in the national interest, Parliament may legislate on a State List subject (valid for 1 year at a time, extendable). (अनुच्छेद 249 के तहत राज्यसभा राष्ट्रीय हित में राज्य सूची के विषय पर संसद को कानून बनाने का अधिकार दे सकती है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 312 is the second exclusive power of Rajya Sabha—authorizing creation of new All-India Services by 2/3rd majority present and voting. (2) Article 250: Parliament legislates on State List during National Emergency. (3) Article 252: Parliament legislates on State List when two or more states pass resolutions requesting it. (4) Article 253: Parliament legislates to implement international treaties.
qe: Under which Article of the Constitution can the Rajya Sabha authorize Parliament to make a law on a State List subject in the national interest?

q:
अनुच्छेद 108 के तहत संसद की संयुक्त बैठक के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: साधारण विधेयक, वित्त विधेयक (श्रेणी I/II) या संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पर गतिरोध दूर करने के लिए संयुक्त बैठक बुलाई जा सकती है।
कथन II: संयुक्त बैठक में विधेयक दोनों सदनों के उपस्थित एवं मतदान करने वाले कुल सदस्यों के साधारण बहुमत से पारित होता है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Statement I is incorrect because a Joint Sitting CANNOT be convened for a Money Bill (Art 110) or a Constitutional Amendment Bill (Art 368). Statement II is correct—decisions in a Joint Sitting are taken by a simple majority of members present and voting. (अतः केवल कथन II सही है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Joint Sitting has been held only 3 times in Indian history: Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978), and Prevention of Terrorism Bill / POTA (2002). (2) Presiding order: Speaker of LS → Deputy Speaker of LS → Deputy Chairman of RS (Chairman of RS / Vice-President NEVER presides over a Joint Sitting).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding a Joint Sitting of Parliament under Article 108:
Statement I: A Joint Sitting can be summoned to resolve a deadlock on an Ordinary Bill, Financial Bill (Category I/II), or a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
Statement II: In a Joint Sitting, the bill is passed by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: निम्नलिखित में से किसे संसद के दोनों सदनों और उनकी समितियों की कार्यवाही में बोलने व भाग लेने का अधिकार है, परंतु मतदान का अधिकार नहीं है?
o: भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक
e: Under Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney General of India (appointed under Article 76) have the right to speak and participate in proceedings of both Houses and any parliamentary committee of which they may be named a member, without a right to vote. (अनुच्छेद 88 के तहत महान्यायवादी को संसद में बोलने का अधिकार है, पर मतदान का नहीं।) Exam Boosters: (1) Attorney General (Art 76) is the highest law officer of India, must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge, and holds office during the pleasure of the President. (2) State counterpart: Advocate General of State under Article 165 (right to speak in State Legislature under Art 177). (3) Solicitor General is a statutory/executive post, NOT a constitutional post.
qe: Who among the following has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament and their committees, without the right to vote?
oe: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: लोकसभा में निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रस्ताव के पारित होने पर मंत्रिपरिषद को अनिवार्य रूप से त्यागपत्र देना पड़ता है और इसे स्वीकार करने हेतु कोई विशिष्ट कारण बताना आवश्यक नहीं है?
e: A No-Confidence Motion (अविश्वास प्रस्ताव, Rule 198 of Lok Sabha) can be moved ONLY in the Lok Sabha with support of at least 50 members, needs no specific reason, is moved against the entire Council of Ministers, and if passed, the government MUST resign. Exam Boosters: (1) Censure Motion (निंदा प्रस्ताव) MUST state reasons, can be moved against an individual minister or the council, and its passage does NOT automatically require resignation (though government usually seeks confidence). (2) Adjournment Motion requires 50 members' support to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance and involves an element of censure. (3) "Zero Hour" (शून्य काल) is an Indian parliamentary innovation since 1962, not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.
qe: Which of the following motions in the Lok Sabha results in the mandatory resignation of the Council of Ministers if passed, and does NOT need to state any specific reason for its adoption?

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत संसद किसी राज्य में विधान परिषद (Legislative Council) का सृजन या उत्सादन कर सकती है?
e: Under Article 169, Parliament may create or abolish a State Legislative Council by simple majority if the concerned State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority (majority of total membership + 2/3rd of members present and voting). (अनुच्छेद 169 के तहत विधान परिषद का सृजन या समाप्ति होती है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Currently 6 Indian states have bicameral legislatures: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. (2) Under Art 171, Council strength cannot exceed 1/3rd of Assembly strength and cannot be less than 40. (3) UP Legislative Council (विधान परिषद) has 100 members and UP Legislative Assembly (विधानसभा) has 403 elected members.
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can Parliament create or abolish a Legislative Council (विधान परिषद) in a State?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 200 के अंतर्गत जब राज्य विधानमंडल द्वारा पारित कोई विधेयक राज्यपाल के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किया जाता है, तो निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प राज्यपाल के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है?
o: विधेयक को राष्ट्रपति के विचारार्थ आरक्षित करना
विधेयक को परामर्श हेतु सीधे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को भेजना
e: Under Article 200, a Governor has four alternatives: assent, withhold assent, return (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or reserve for the President's consideration (mandatory if the Bill endangers the position of the High Court). Only the President (under Art 143)—NOT the Governor—can seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion. Exam Boosters: (1) Once reserved for the President (Art 201), the Governor has no further role, and the President is NOT bound to assent even if the State Legislature passes the Bill a second time. (2) Unlike the President, the Governor cannot summon a Joint Sitting of the State Legislature—there is NO provision for a Joint Sitting in states.
qe: Under Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, when a Bill passed by a State Legislature is presented to the Governor, which of the following is NOT one of the options available to the Governor?
oe: Reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President
Refer the Bill directly to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion

q: केंद्र-राज्य संबंधों की कार्यप्रणाली की समीक्षा हेतु भारत सरकार द्वारा 1983 में किस आयोग का गठन किया गया था?
e: The Sarkaria Commission (chaired by Justice R. S. Sarkaria, with B. Sivaraman and S. R. Sen) was appointed in 1983 and submitted its 1988 report with 247 recommendations, including establishing a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263 (set up in 1990). Exam Boosters: (1) Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by the Tamil Nadu government. (2) Punchhi Commission (2007–2010, chaired by Justice M. M. Punchhi) was the second major Centre-State commission. (3) Legislative relations are in Part XI (Art 245–255), Administrative in Part XI (Art 256–263), and Financial in Part XII (Art 268–293).
qe: Which Commission was appointed in 1983 by the Government of India to examine and review the working of Centre-State relations?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा अनुच्छेद 352 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल की घोषणा के आधार के रूप में "आंतरिक अशांति" के स्थान पर "सशस्त्र विद्रोह" शब्द प्रतिस्थापित किया गया?
e: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 replaced "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion", required written recommendation of the Union Cabinet for Art 352, reduced parliamentary approval time from 2 months to 1 month, and required special majority for approval. (44वें संशोधन 1978 द्वारा "आंतरिक अशांति" को "सशस्त्र विद्रोह" से बदला गया।) Exam Boosters: (1) National Emergency (Art 352) has been proclaimed 3 times: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Pakistan war), and 1975 (internal disturbance). (2) Art 358 automatically suspends Art 19 ONLY during external emergency (war/external aggression), NOT armed rebellion. (3) Financial Emergency (Art 360) has NEVER been declared in India.
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment replaced the phrase "internal disturbance" (आंतरिक अशांति) with "armed rebellion" (सशस्त्र विद्रोह) as a ground for declaring National Emergency under Article 352?

q: अनुच्छेद 356 (राष्ट्रपति शासन) के अंतर्गत किसी राज्य में राष्ट्रपति शासन अधिकतम कितनी अवधि तक लागू रह सकता है तथा इसे एक वर्ष से अधिक बढ़ाने के लिए कौन-सी शर्तें आवश्यक हैं?
o: 2 वर्ष; हर 6 माह में साधारण बहुमत
3 वर्ष; राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल लागू हो तथा निर्वाचन आयोग प्रमाणित करे कि चुनाव संभव नहीं
3 वर्ष; केवल राज्यसभा के 2/3 बहुमत से
हर 6 माह में संसदीय स्वीकृति के साथ अनिश्चितकाल तक
e: President's Rule (Art 356) must be approved by both Houses by simple majority within 2 months, lasts 6 months at a time, and can be extended up to a maximum of 3 years. Under the 44th Amendment, extension beyond 1 year is permitted ONLY if BOTH conditions are met: (i) National Emergency is in operation in India/state, AND (ii) Election Commission certifies that Assembly elections cannot be held. Exam Boosters: (1) In S. R. Bommai Case (1994), SC held Art 356 proclamation is subject to judicial review, secularism is part of Basic Structure, and floor test in Assembly is the only valid test of majority. (2) Maximum period of National Emergency (Art 352) is indefinite (renewed every 6 months).
qe: Under Article 356 (President's Rule), what is the maximum period for which President's Rule can remain in force in a State, and what conditions apply for extending it beyond ONE year?
oe: 2 years; simple majority approval every 6 months
3 years; National Emergency in force AND Election Commission certifies elections cannot be held
3 years; approval by 2/3rd majority of Rajya Sabha only
Indefinitely with parliamentary approval every 6 months

q: केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच समन्वय बढ़ाने हेतु राष्ट्रपति द्वारा अंतर्राज्यीय परिषद (Inter-State Council) की स्थापना किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत की जाती है?
e: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council (chaired by the Prime Minister, with all State CMs, UT CMs/Administrators, and 6 Union Cabinet Ministers). (अनुच्छेद 263 अंतर्राज्यीय परिषद से संबंधित है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 262: Adjudication of inter-state river water disputes (Parliament enacted Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956). (2) Article 279A (101st Amendment, 2016): Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister. (3) Zonal Councils (5 statutory bodies + North-Eastern Council) are NOT constitutional bodies; they were created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and chaired by the Union Home Minister.
qe: Under which Article is the Inter-State Council established by the President to promote coordination between the Centre and the States?

q: अनुच्छेद 279A के अंतर्गत जीएसटी परिषद (GST Council) में केंद्र सरकार तथा सभी राज्य सरकारों के सम्मिलित मतों का भारांश (weightage) कितना है और निर्णय के लिए कितना बहुमत आवश्यक है?
e: Under Article 279A(9), every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of NOT LESS than 3/4th (75%) of the weighted votes of members present and voting, where the Central Government has 1/3rd weightage and all State Governments taken together have 2/3rd weightage. (केंद्र 1/3, राज्य 2/3 तथा निर्णय 3/4 बहुमत से।) Exam Boosters: (1) Quorum of GST Council is 1/2 (50%) of total members. (2) GST was introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 (implemented from 1 July 2017). (3) In Mohit Minerals Case (2022), SC held GST Council recommendations have persuasive value and are not strictly binding on Parliament/States.
qe: Regarding the GST Council under Article 279A, what is the weightage of the Central Government's vote and the State Governments' combined votes, and what majority is required for a decision?
oe: Centre 1/3, States 2/3; decision by simple majority

q: उच्चतर न्यायालय द्वारा किसी लोक प्राधिकारी या अधिकारी को उस सार्वजनिक कर्तव्य का पालन करने का आदेश देने हेतु कौन-सी रिट जारी की जाती है जिसे करने से उसने इनकार किया हो?
e: Mandamus literally means "We Command" (हम आदेश देते हैं); it directs a public official, public body, corporation, or inferior court to perform a legal public duty. It CANNOT be issued against a private individual, the President, or State Governors. Exam Boosters: (1) Habeas Corpus ("to have the body of"): Protects individual liberty against illegal detention (can be issued against BOTH public authorities and private individuals). (2) Prohibition ("to forbid"): Issued by higher court to lower court/tribunal to prevent exceeding jurisdiction (preventive). (3) Certiorari ("to be certified"): Issued to quash an order already passed by a lower court/tribunal (preventive + curative). (4) Quo Warranto ("by what authority"): Challenges legality of a person's claim to a public office.
qe: Which writ is issued by a higher court to a public authority or official commanding them to perform a public duty that they have failed or refused to perform?

q: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश तथा उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश की सेवानिवृत्ति की आयु क्रमशः कितनी है?
e: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 years (Art 124), whereas High Court judges retire at 62 years (Art 217; raised from 60 to 62 by the 15th Amendment Act, 1963). (सुप्रीम कोर्ट: 65 वर्ष; हाई कोर्ट: 62 वर्ष।) Exam Boosters: (1) The Constitution prescribes NO minimum age for appointment as SC or HC judge. (2) Judges of SC and HC are removed by the President only after an address by both Houses of Parliament passed by special majority on grounds of "proved misbehaviour or incapacity" [Art 124(4)]. (3) Allahabad High Court (established 1866 at Agra, shifted to Allahabad in 1869) is the largest High Court in India by sanctioned judge strength.
qe: What is the retirement age of a Judge of the Supreme Court of India and a Judge of a High Court respectively?

q: किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच अथवा राज्यों के आपसी संघीय विवादों में "प्रारंभिक एवं अनन्य अधिकारिता" का प्रयोग करता है?
e: Article 131 grants Original and Exclusive Jurisdiction to the Supreme Court in federal disputes (Centre vs State, Centre+State vs State, State vs State) involving a question of law or fact on which a legal right depends. (अनुच्छेद 131 सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की प्रारंभिक अधिकारिता से संबंधित है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 129: Supreme Court as a Court of Record (with power to punish for contempt); High Court as Court of Record is Art 215. (2) Article 136: Special Leave Petition (SLP). (3) Article 137: Review of judgments by Supreme Court. (4) Article 143: Advisory Jurisdiction of SC on President's reference.
qe: Under which Article does the Supreme Court exercise "Original and Exclusive Jurisdiction" in federal disputes between the Centre and one or more States, or between two or more States?

q: निम्नलिखित न्यायाधीशों में से किसे भारत में जनहित याचिका (PIL) का जनक/प्रणेता माना जाता है?
e: Justice P. N. Bhagwati (along with Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer) pioneered Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India in the late 1970s–1980s, relaxing the traditional rule of "locus standi" so public-spirited citizens could approach courts on behalf of marginalized groups. Exam Boosters: (1) Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979) is considered the first major PIL case (speedy trial of undertrial prisoners). (2) S. P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981) formally articulated the principles of PIL. (3) PIL can be filed ONLY in the Supreme Court (Art 32) or High Courts (Art 226), NOT in subordinate courts.
qe: Who among the following judges is widely regarded as the pioneer of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India?

q: कौन-सा अनुच्छेद सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को उसके समक्ष लंबित किसी मामले में "पूर्ण न्याय" (complete justice) करने के लिए आवश्यक डिक्री या आदेश पारित करने की शक्ति देता है?
e: Article 142 grants extraordinary plenary power to the Supreme Court to do "complete justice" in any matter before it (used in cases like Ayodhya verdict, Union Carbide/Bhopal Gas, and irretrievable breakdown of marriage). (अनुच्छेद 142 सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को पूर्ण न्याय की शक्ति देता है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 141: Law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India. (2) Article 144: All civil and judicial authorities in India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court. (3) Article 145: Rules of Court (a Constitution Bench requires a minimum of 5 judges under Art 145(3)).
qe: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing "complete justice" in any cause or matter pending before it?

q:
भारत में उच्च न्यायालयों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: अनुच्छेद 227 के अंतर्गत उच्च न्यायालय को अपने क्षेत्राधिकार के सभी न्यायालयों व अधिकरणों (सैन्य अधिकरणों सहित) पर अधीक्षण की शक्ति प्राप्त है।
कथन II: अनुच्छेद 231 के अंतर्गत संसद विधि द्वारा दो या अधिक राज्यों के लिए एक साझा उच्च न्यायालय स्थापित कर सकती है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: न तो I और न ही II
e: Statement I is incorrect because Article 227(4) explicitly EXCLUDES courts or tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces (military tribunals). Statement II is correct—Article 231 (amended by 7th Amendment Act, 1956) authorizes Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more States or States and UTs. (अतः केवल कथन II सही है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Currently India has 25 High Courts (Andhra Pradesh HC at Amaravati being the 25th, 2019). (2) Delhi and Jammu & Kashmir are the only UTs with their own separate High Courts. (3) Salaries of HC judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, whereas their PENSIONS are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India!
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the High Courts in India:
Statement I: Under Article 227, a High Court exercises power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout its territorial jurisdiction, including military tribunals.
Statement II: Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States under Article 231.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: 1957 में भारत में त्रिस्तरीय पंचायती राज व्यवस्था (ग्राम पंचायत, पंचायत समिति, जिला परिषद) की सिफारिश किस समिति ने की थी?
e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended democratic decentralization via a 3-tier Panchayati Raj structure, first inaugurated by PM Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur (Rajasthan), followed by Andhra Pradesh. Exam Boosters: (1) Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a 2-tier system (Zila Parishad & Mandal Panchayat). (2) L. M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj, realized by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (effective 24 April 1993 — National Panchayati Raj Day). (3) PESA Act, 1996 extended Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule tribal areas.
qe: Which committee recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system (Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad) in India in 1957?

q: 73वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 (भाग IX) के अंतर्गत निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सभी राज्यों के लिए एक अनिवार्य (mandatory) प्रावधान है?
o: पिछड़ा वर्ग के लिए सीटों का आरक्षण
महिलाओं के लिए सीटों व अध्यक्ष पदों का न्यूनतम 1/3 आरक्षण
पंचायतों में सांसदों व विधायकों को प्रतिनिधित्व देना
पंचायतों को सभी राज्य कर लगाने का अधिकार देना
e: Under Article 243D, reserving not less than 1/3rd of total seats AND chairperson offices at all levels for women (and proportional reservation for SCs/STs) is mandatory. Reservation for OBCs, MP/MLA representation, and taxing powers are voluntary/discretionary provisions left to State Legislatures. Exam Boosters: (1) Other mandatory provisions of 73rd Amendment: Gram Sabha (Art 243A), 5-year fixed tenure & fresh elections within 6 months of dissolution (Art 243E), minimum age 21 years to contest (Art 243F), State Finance Commission every 5 years (Art 243I), and State Election Commission (Art 243K). (2) States with population under 20 lakh need not constitute the intermediate tier.
qe: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IX), which of the following is a MANDATORY (compulsory) provision for all states?
oe: Reservation of seats for Backward Classes
Minimum 1/3rd reservation of seats and chairperson posts for women
Giving representation to MPs and MLAs in Panchayats
Authorizing Panchayats to levy and collect all state taxes

q: संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति द्वारा भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) की नियुक्ति की जाती है?
e: Article 148 provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, appointed by the President for a term of 6 years or up to age 65, whichever is earlier. (अनुच्छेद 148 भारत के CAG से संबंधित है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the CAG "probably the most important officer in the Constitution of India". (2) CAG is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge and is ineligible for any further office under the Union or State governments after retirement. (3) CAG submits audit reports to the President (Art 151) and Governors, and acts as "friend, philosopher, and guide" to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
qe: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India appointed by the President?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा लोकसभा और राज्य विधानसभा चुनावों में मतदान की न्यूनतम आयु 21 वर्ष से घटाकर 18 वर्ष कर दी गई?
e: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (effective 28 March 1989) amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18 years for universal adult suffrage. (61वें संशोधन 1988 द्वारा मतदान की आयु 21 से 18 वर्ष की गई।) Exam Boosters: (1) 69th Amendment Act, 1991 accorded special status to Delhi as the National Capital Territory (NCT) with a 70-member Legislative Assembly and 7-member Council of Ministers (Art 239AA). (2) Election Commission of India (Art 324) became a 3-member multi-member body permanently in October 1993. (3) National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25 January (ECI foundation day, 25 Jan 1950).
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the minimum voting age in Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा निकाय भारतीय संविधान के अंतर्गत एक संवैधानिक निकाय (Constitutional Body) नहीं है?
e: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is an extra-constitutional (non-constitutional and non-statutory) executive body created by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (1950). (नीति आयोग एक गैर-संवैधानिक निकाय है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Finance Commission: Constitutional body under Article 280 (16th Finance Commission chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya). (2) UPSC: Constitutional body under Article 315 (members serve 6 years or up to age 65; State PSC members up to age 62). (3) NCBC: Given constitutional status under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 (alongside NCSC Art 338 and NCST Art 338A).
qe: Which of the following bodies is NOT a Constitutional Body under the Indian Constitution?

q:
सूची-I (हालिया संविधान संशोधन) को सूची-II (विषय) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. 103वाँ संशोधन, 2019 — (a) लोकसभा व विधानसभाओं में 33% महिला आरक्षण
2. 104वाँ संशोधन, 2019 — (b) शिक्षा व नौकरियों में 10% EWS आरक्षण
3. 105वाँ संशोधन, 2021 — (c) राज्यों को SEBC/OBC पहचानने की शक्ति बहाल
4. 106वाँ संशोधन, 2023 — (d) आंग्ल-भारतीय मनोनयन समाप्त; SC/ST आरक्षण विस्तार
e: 103rd Amendment (2019) introduced 10% EWS quota via Art 15(6) & 16(6) (1-b); 104th Amendment (2019) extended SC/ST legislative reservation by 10 years up to 2030 and discontinued Anglo-Indian nominations under Art 331/333 (2-d); 105th Amendment (2021) restored States' power to maintain their own OBC lists (3-c); and 106th Amendment (2023, Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Assembly via Art 330A/332A (4-a).
qe:
Match List-I (Recent Constitutional Amendment) with List-II (Subject):
1. 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 — (a) Women's Reservation (33%) in Lok Sabha & State Assemblies
2. 104th Amendment Act, 2019 — (b) 10% EWS Reservation in education & jobs
3. 105th Amendment Act, 2021 — (c) Restored States' power to identify SEBCs/OBCs
4. 106th Amendment Act, 2023 — (d) Ended Anglo-Indian nomination; extended SC/ST reservation

q: 74वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 (भाग IXA) के अंतर्गत कौन-सा अनुच्छेद पंचायतों व नगरपालिकाओं द्वारा तैयार योजनाओं को समेकित करने हेतु "जिला योजना समिति" के गठन का प्रावधान करता है?
e: Article 243ZD mandates a District Planning Committee (DPC) in every district, where at least 4/5ths of members must be elected by and from the elected members of the district-level Panchayat and Municipalities in proportion to rural-urban population. (अनुच्छेद 243ZD जिला योजना समिति से संबंधित है।) Exam Boosters: (1) Article 243ZE: Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC), where at least 2/3rds of members are elected. (2) Article 243W: Powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities (18 subjects in 12th Schedule). (3) Article 243Q: Three types of Municipalities—Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.
qe: Under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IXA), which Article provides for the constitution of a "District Planning Committee" (जिला योजना समिति) to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities?

q: अनुच्छेद 368 के अंतर्गत निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रावधान में संशोधन के लिए संसद के विशेष बहुमत के साथ-साथ कम से कम आधे राज्य विधानमंडलों का अनुसमर्थन (ratification) भी आवश्यक है?
o: भाग III के मौलिक अधिकारों में परिवर्तन
भाग IV के नीति निदेशक तत्वों में परिवर्तन
अनुच्छेद 54 व 55 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति के निर्वाचन की रीति
अनुच्छेद 169 के अंतर्गत विधान परिषद का सृजन या उत्सादन
e: Federal provisions listed in the proviso to Article 368(2)—including election of the President (Art 54, 55), extent of Union/State executive power (Art 73, 162), Supreme Court & High Courts, Seventh Schedule lists, GST Council (Art 279A), representation of states in Parliament, and Article 368 itself—require special majority of Parliament PLUS ratification by at least half the State Legislatures (by simple majority). Exam Boosters: (1) Fundamental Rights and DPSP require special majority of Parliament ONLY (no state ratification). (2) Art 169 (Legislative Council) requires only a simple majority of Parliament (outside Art 368). (3) By the 24th Amendment Act (1971), it is obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill (no veto power).
qe: Under Article 368, which of the following provisions requires BOTH a special majority of Parliament AND ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures?
oe: Alteration of Fundamental Rights in Part III
Changes to Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Manner of election of the President under Articles 54 and 55
Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils under Article 169
